sources.citation: Austin, Peter. 1988. Phonological voicing contrasts in Australian Aboriginal languages. La Trobe Working Papers in Linguistics 1: 17-42.
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Sec. 3.3 'Western Queensland': Warluwarra voiced stops follow phonetically long vowels, voiceless after short (Breen 1971a:22, Dixon 1980:215); contrast not significant for velars. Nothing on Warluwarra stress placement. For sister language Bularnu it quotes Breen (1974:5) 'the stressed (i.e. first) vowel in a disyllabic word is long if the following consonant is a voiced stop' -- i.e. initial stress in Bularnu, not stated for Warluwarra. (Internet Archive copy of the PDF is truncated; text recovered from the content streams.)
